hints: Look at who is donating the proton in this hydrolysis, the hydrated aluminium ion or the water molecule.
Remember a conjugate pair differs by exactly one $H^+$ and appears on opposite sides of the equation.
Think about what added $OH^-$ will do to the $H_3O^+$ on the right, and how Le Chatelier responds to removing a product.
walkthrough:
**Spot the acid and base**

This is hydrolysis of a highly charged $Al^{3+}$ ion. The $Al^{3+}$ polarises the O-H bonds in its water ligands so strongly that a water ligand releases $H^+$.

$$[Al(H_2O)_6]^{3+}(aq) + H_2O(l) \rightleftharpoons [Al(H_2O)_5OH]^{2+}(aq) + H_3O^+(aq)$$

**Identify the true conjugate pairs**

By Bronsted-Lowry theory, an acid donates $H^+$ to become its conjugate base. So the pairs are linked across the arrow.

$$[Al(H_2O)_6]^{3+} / [Al(H_2O)_5OH]^{2+} \text{ and } H_3O^+ / H_2O$$

**Apply Le Chatelier with added alkali**

If $OH^-(aq)$ is added, it neutralises the $H_3O^+$ product:
$$H_3O^+(aq) + OH^-(aq) \rightarrow 2H_2O(l)$$
Removing a product pulls the equilibrium to the right to replace it.

**Remember what Kc depends on**

$K_c$ is constant at constant temperature. Changing concentration or pH changes the position of equilibrium, not the value of $K_c$.

options.A: Incorrect. A conjugate pair must differ by one $H^+$ and be related by donation. $[Al(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ and $[Al(H_2O)_5OH]^{2+}$ are a pair, and $H_3O^+$ and $H_2O$ are the other pair. $H_2O$ and $[Al(H_2O)_5OH]^{2+}$ are both bases in different pairs.
options.B: Incorrect. Here $H_2O(l)$ accepts $H^+$ to form $H_3O^+$, so it is acting as a Bronsted-Lowry base. It is the $[Al(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ ion that donates $H^+$ and acts as the acid.
options.C: Correct. Added $OH^-$ removes $H_3O^+$ by neutralisation. By Le Chatelier's principle, the system shifts right to make more $H_3O^+$ and more $[Al(H_2O)_5OH]^{2+}$. This is why $Al^{3+}$ solutions become more hydrolysed in alkali.
options.D: Incorrect. $K_c$ only changes with temperature. Varying pH by adding acid or alkali changes concentrations and shifts the position of equilibrium, but the value of $K_c$ stays the same.
